correctness.rationale: PASS: Directly reconstructed the shortest-span consecutive-one gap criterion for every r=1..6 (including r=1,6), the four nontrivial offset inequalities and their exact partition into d>=b and d<b. The rational sums are valid as formal series; independent SymPy cross-multiplication reduced H_ge+H_lt-A/((1-z^3)(1-z^4)^2(1-z^6)^2) to identically zero, not just finitely many coefficients. A(1)=867 gives order-seven pole 289/3456; A mod Phi_4=z, A mod Phi_6=1 ensures order-four and order-six primitive poles, forcing period 12. Direct independent brute prefix-normal enumeration for n=7..14 gave 1,4,13,31,71,134,249,417. All n is justified by algebra, not finite enumeration.

value.rationale: PASS: Fixed-one-count rationality is known in general, but evaluating the first explicit density beyond an established six-one table gives a precise natural language enumerator, a non-obvious palindromic numerator, period twelve and sharp leading coefficient. These are independently useful to fixed-content word enumeration; no claim about all densities is needed.

limitations: Only length-variable binary prefix-normal words with exactly seven ones; no all-density expression.
Finite word checks are corroboration, not an unbounded proof.
